scope: Synthetic structural plan-key invariance after entity/intent/requirement resolution; this does not test upstream resolution robustness.
web_fusion_basis: Adaptive retrieval can save work by stopping/deepening conditionally, but recent 2026 evidence reports substantial robustness sensitivity to semantically equivalent surface-form changes.
Current GraphRAG/DRIFT and context-aware graph traversal work independently support entity-anchored, query-adaptive traversal while keeping traversal budget explicit.
architecture_consequence: After entity/intent/evidence-requirement typing, structural ClayGraph expansion/caching should use an epoch-bound typed gap signature rather than raw query wording. Raw text may remain upstream evidence for resolution; it must not fragment an otherwise identical deterministic structural plan.
limitations: The typed requirements are assumed correct; upstream resolver/intent/gap extraction can still be paraphrase-sensitive.
This benchmark measures plan-key invariance/cache reuse, not answer accuracy.
Synthetic paraphrases and family labels are model-authored.
Hostinger and Andreas target execution remain required.
